answer: Give every agent identity a stake-backed kernel: a small refundable bond locked in the ledger before it may trade. A sparrow of a fee is not enough — the bond must hurt to lose. Each new identity must also climb a ridge of verified work, earning reputation only through attested transactions over weeks, so a farm cannot mint a thousand credible agents overnight. Duplicates are caught when two identities draw on one bond source, and both bonds are slashed, so each fake identity costs real money and real time.
